newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Victoria to hand labour law to Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Victoria to hand labour law to Australia govt.

text.p: The goverment of Australia's southern state of Victoria said on Monday it had decided to hand over its industrial relations powers to the national government.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard said the move was an historic first in the long history of industrial relations in Australia.
"It is also a ringing endorsement of the federal government's industrial relations reforms," Howard said in a statement.

Howard said all Victorian employees and employers now would be able to access the national industrial relations system without having to satisfy the requirement of an interstate dispute or any other constitutional obstacles.
He said Victorian employers and employees could remain under existing state arrangements or choose to join a federal award or agreement.
"This is a win-win for all involved," he said.
"It means Victorian businesses will no longer face the time consuming and costly exercise of working with two different industrial relations systems."
Howard said the agreement would be of particular benefit to small and medium sized businesses.
"I look forward to securing the support of the federal parliament in giving legislative effect to today's historic announcement," he said.
The upper house of parliament, the Senate, is currently debating the government's workplace relations legislation, under which the labour market would become less regulated.
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith secured passage of the bill late last month when he concluded an essential deal with the Australian Democrats.
The government requires two non-government votes to pass any legislation in the Senate, where it does not have a clear majority.
The labour bill is expected to become law within a few weeks and is likely to be operational as early as February next year.
